newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indian state seeks investments in infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: Indian state seeks investments in infrastructure.

text.p: India's most industrialised state, Maharashtra, is seeking private investment in 55 infrastructure projects, a senior state government official said on Tuesday.
Sureshdada Jain, Maharashtra's minister for trade and commerce, said feasibility studies for the projects had already been completed and the necessary approval obtained.

Foreign investors have shown the most interest in the state's power, port, road and housing sectors, Jain told a news conference on the last day of a two-week business mission to Taiwan, Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore.
The estimated value of the projects exceeds US$5 billion.
Jain said the projects would also be promoted at a three-day global investors conference in Bombay next month.
On the long-delayed $600 million tie-up between Singapore Airlines and India's Tata group, Jain said he believed the proposed deal should be approved.

"My personal decision is it (approval) should be given. The Maharashtra government welcomes foreign investment and privatisation," he said, noting however, the decision ultimately rested with the federal government.
SIA and Tata Industries Ltd submitted their proposal to launch a domestic Indian airline in February 1995.
The Tatas were planning to hold a 60 percent stake, with SIA owning the rest.
Since then, the proposal has been held up by a government dispute over whether to permit foreign investment in the aviation sector.
The Indian government on Friday approved a domestic aviation policy allowing foreign investors to take stakes of up to 40 percent in domestic airlines.
But it deferred a key decision on whether to allow foreign airlines or airport companies to participate directly in the equity holding of domestic counterparts.
